Six, Marina, Nine, Adam, Sam, and Malcolm each take on a part of the effort, from training human Garde to reading the Mogadorian order of battle. The occupation itself is entrenched: the Mogadorians hold ground in cities across the planet and can reinforce from orbit, and no counterattack yet attempted has held anything for long.

Number Five gives himself up to the Garde. He is imprisoned rather than executed, over John's objections, because what he knows about Setrakus Ra, the fleet, and the Mogadorian command is not available anywhere else. Nobody in the group trusts a word of it, and everybody uses it. For John the arrangement is intolerable: Five killed Number Eight and John holds him responsible for Sarah, and he has to work with the intelligence anyway. Meanwhile Ella's connection to Setrakus Ra persists even at a distance, which makes her the Garde's best window into what he intends and a standing risk to every plan they make in her presence.

The alliance goes onto the offensive, retaking ground and hitting Mogadorian positions with a mix of human forces, Loric Garde, and the human Garde whose Legacies arrived weeks ago and who are being sent into combat with almost no training. The victories are real and expensive. Adam's knowledge of Mogadorian ships and command structures shapes the campaign, and Sam's ability to reach machines becomes a weapon in its own right. Throughout, the strategic problem stays unsolved: every Mogadorian position can be taken, and none of it matters while Setrakus Ra is alive, because he cannot be killed by anything the Garde have brought against him.

The Garde work out the shape of the problem they have been avoiding. Setrakus Ra survives injuries that would kill anything else, and the claim he made on Ella has left the two of them connected, so that harming him may kill her. Any plan that ends the war therefore has to solve both at once, and the only person developing fast enough to attempt it is John, whose Legacies have kept expanding until he can take on powers he watches other people use. He does not tell the others what that is likely to cost. The alliance commits to a final assault on Setrakus Ra himself rather than continuing to fight the occupation position by position.

The final assault reaches Setrakus Ra. The fighting costs the alliance heavily, and the Garde and human Garde together are able to bring the Mogadorian leader within reach but not to kill him. John, carrying more Legacies than any of them, breaks the link that protected him and destroys him, and dies doing it. Ella survives, released from the claim Setrakus Ra made on her. With their leader dead, the Mogadorian occupation collapses and the invasion ends. Six, Marina, Nine, Sam, Adam, and Malcolm survive, and so do the human Garde. What the survivors are left with is a planet full of people who now have Legacies, a war won at the cost of the person who held them together, and the question of what happens to the powers Lorien gave away.

characters.description: The leader of Omega Force, a small independent crew that takes on dangerous operations.
characters.name: Jason Burke

characters.description: Omega Force's highly capable battle synth and principal combatant.
characters.name: Lucky

characters.description: The name by which a contract broker knew Lucky during earlier work. The broker recognizes him during Omega Force's inquiry into the border trafficking network, and Lucky confirms that he now uses a different name.
characters.name: Seven

characters.description: Seven's former contract broker and a source on the border trafficking network. The broker tells Omega Force that competing cartels supply captives to a larger buyer.
characters.name: Contract broker

characters.description: A trafficking collector at the Gates and a survivor of Seven's earlier attack on another criminal organization. He accepts the apparently inactive synth as a trophy during Omega Force's infiltration.
characters.name: The Butcher

characters.description: Lucky's former military designation, recognized aboard the ship treating Cage. The identification connects his current life and the name Seven to his earlier existence as a combat unit.
characters.name: Combat Unit 777

characters.description: Omega Force's intelligence and network specialist. He supports field missions through surveillance, data recovery, security bypasses, and system intrusion.
characters.name: Cage

characters.description: Omega Force's combat specialist and a formidable close-quarters fighter.
characters.name: Crusher

characters.description: Crusher's formal identity as Guardian Archon of Galvatore. Jason learns the title while confronting the consequences of Doc's unauthorized treatment and the danger that discovery would pose.
characters.name: Felix Tezakar

characters.description: Omega Force's medic.
characters.name: Doc

characters.description: Omega Force's engineer.
characters.name: Twingo

characters.description: A covert operative, Carolyn Whitney's partner, and Shira's father. He relies on Omega Force to extract his daughter when Cridal personnel compromise her Earth safe house.
characters.name: Abia

characters.description: Abia's ten-year-old daughter and the objective of Omega Force's Earth extraction. Cridal personnel are watching her safe house, forcing the crew to abandon the planned route and evacuate immediately.
characters.name: Shira Mizrahi

characters.description: An assassin, Abia's partner, and the true target of the Cridal operation that used Shira as bait. She separates from Abia and Shira to draw the threat away from them.
characters.name: Carolyn Whitney

characters.description: Jason's retired associate on Earth. He activates contacts in a sleeper network, secures passage off-world for Omega Force and Shira, and uses concealed defenses to hinder the pursuing Cridal team.
characters.name: Russ Johnson

characters.description: The premier of Cridal. Her fixation on Carolyn Whitney is worsening a leadership crisis and has helped bring diplomatic consequences after the failed operation on Earth.
characters.name: Crisstof Dalton

characters.description: A senior Cridal official trying to contain the political damage caused by Crisstof Dalton's deterioration. The official seeks a private meeting with Earth's ambassador while assessing the Cooperative's leadership crisis.
characters.name: Cridal chief of staff

characters.description: An injured local opportunist known to the crew who claims to have intelligence about cartel cash movements. Omega Force takes him aboard at Kefen-6 for treatment and questioning.
characters.name: Injured former associate

characters.description: An Esquarian intelligence minister and an ally of Omega Force who has resumed his original identity. He offers Jason limited intelligence support for the border trafficking inquiry while warning of greater dangers.
characters.name: Saditava Mok

characters.description: An Esquarian naval commander and protected flag officer. Esquarian intelligence refuses a Cridal request to remove her, leaving the purpose behind that request uncertain.
characters.name: Kellea Colleren

characters.description: The regional director of the trafficking network. Scarred and in chronic pain, this planner treats losses as replaceable, strengthens security after Omega Force's raids, and prepares an evacuation contingency.
characters.name: Trafficking-ring leader

characters.description: The designation assigned by Esquarian intelligence to the captured regional trafficking director. He is transferred into their custody along with evidence from the broken Gates operation.
characters.name: P9971

characters.description: An Esquarian ministerial contact who receives Jason's evidence that a former regional military officer is directing high-level trafficking. The information is elevated for government review.
characters.name: Esquarian government contact

characters.description: A juvenile survivor separated from her refugee family by the traffickers' transport system. Distrusting local authorities, she hides in Omega Force's vehicle and describes the repeated scanning, sorting, and transfers used on captives.
characters.name: Andal

characters.description: A capable newcomer within the Gates cartel whose rapid rise attracts suspicion from the regional trafficking director. His loyalty and purpose are unclear when he first enters the operation.
characters.name: Cartel subordinate

characters.description: A Naval Intelligence Service agent who has been operating undercover inside the Gates cartel. He turns the trafficking director's escape into a trap and offers to help Jason and Crusher capture him alive.
characters.name: Bill Ackerman

characters.description: An armed synth escort and an associate from Lucky's distant military past. Officially believed dismantled after ordering a massacre, the unit is now serving the operator who takes control of Cage's treatment.
characters.name: Combat Unit P002

characters.description: A private operator with access to advanced medical care and recruitment contacts in fringe space. The employer continues Cage's treatment but makes Lucky responsible for the resulting, unspecified debt.
characters.name: Visselo employer

characters.description: An ally of Jason who receives the captured trafficking director and Bill Ackerman. Their friendship followed an initially hostile history, and Webb now helps route the prisoner and intelligence to allied channels.
characters.name: Marcus Webb

characters.description: A battle synth ally who volunteers to join Jason's pursuit of Lucky and Cage. Despite personal friction between them, the unit believes they can cooperate effectively as soldiers.
characters.name: Combat Unit 701

characters.description: A sentient AI database tied to Jason. After earlier damage, it has rebuilt much of its interface and now contributes engineering designs for the Phoenix's extensive reconstruction.
characters.name: The Archive

description.text: Continuing the series, Omega Force extracts a child, Shira, from a compromised safe house before her Cridal Red Strike pursuers can use her as bait against a hidden target: Carolyn Whitney, who ends her relationship with Shira's father to keep him and Shira safe. After delivering the family to refuge, the crew turns to investigating a growing slave-trafficking network destabilizing the border regions, following leads from a broker connected to Seven's criminal past. An elaborate deception plants an apparently deactivated Lucky inside a trafficking collector's compound to steal operational data on the network's depots, while the rival Cridal Cooperative faces a worsening leadership crisis of its own. With the stolen intelligence, Omega Force commits to striking the largest identified trafficking depot.

recaps.ending: Omega Force breaks the Gates cartel and captures its regional director, who enters Esquarian custody as P9971. The recovered intelligence and a Cridal special-operations shuttle support the conclusion that a network inside Cridal was involved, although the larger organizer, destination, and purpose of the trafficking remain unknown. Cage survives a near-fatal attack but is still receiving treatment aboard a departing private frigate. Lucky stays with him and accepts an unspecified obligation to their captors, then warns Jason against following. Jason nevertheless leaves in the SX-5 with Combat Unit 701 to find them. The Phoenix remains dismantled for reconstruction on Satora, where Twingo stays with the work and the Archive assists. Crusher is physically restored, but disclosure of his treatment could bring deadly political consequences. Andal and Shira are safe with Abia. Crisstof Dalton orders an investigation into the rogue network within her government, while Carolyn Whitney resumes her contract to kill Dalton. Kellea Colleren's possible wider campaign against the cartels and Whitney's separate contract concerning her remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After extracting Abia's daughter Shira from a Cridal operation on Earth, Omega Force investigates an industrial trafficking network in the border region. Raids reveal a coordinated system moving vast numbers of refugees for an unknown purpose, while the Phoenix is crippled and Crusher secretly undergoes dangerous genetic treatment. At the Gates, the crew discovers tens of thousands of captives and a covert Cridal connection. Cage is critically wounded, and Lucky accepts an unknown debt to secure his treatment before both are carried away aboard a private frigate. Jason, Crusher, and undercover agent Bill Ackerman capture the regional director, later designated P9971, and deliver him and the evidence to allied Esquarian channels. The wider network remains active. With the Phoenix undergoing a major rebuild, Jason and Combat Unit 701 depart in the SX-5 to pursue Lucky and Cage. Crisstof Dalton begins investigating the unauthorized network in her government just as Carolyn Whitney resumes her contract to kill her.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Burke leads Omega Force, an independent crew. Its returning members include Lucky, a highly capable battle synth; Cage, an intelligence and network specialist; Crusher, a combat specialist; Doc, the crew's medic; and Twingo, its engineer. They travel aboard the Phoenix and bring combat, technical, medical, and intelligence capabilities to their operations. These people and roles are already in place when the new operation begins.

Omega Force extracts ten-year-old Shira Mizrahi from an Earth safe house after Cridal personnel close in. Lucky learns that she is bait intended to draw out Carolyn Whitney, an assassin known as the Viper and the partner of Shira's father, Abia. Jason's retired associate Russ Johnson secures an alternate route off-world, and Abia reunites with his daughter. Whitney separates from them to draw the danger away. After recovering the Phoenix, Omega Force turns to the growing slave trade in the border region. A former broker identifies Lucky as Seven and explains that several cartels feed captives to a larger buyer. At the Gates, the crew infiltrates a collector's compound, secretly copies operational data, and escapes without exposing the theft. The information identifies missing people and trafficking depots, giving Omega Force targets for a direct campaign. Meanwhile, Cridal premier Crisstof Dalton faces diplomatic pressure over the failed Earth operation, while her chief of staff quietly approaches Esquarian intelligence about Kellea Colleren.

Omega Force attacks the largest identified depot. The Phoenix suffers severe engine damage but destroys the site's defenses, and the ground team seizes a freighter built to carry hundreds of prisoners. The network's regional director responds by strengthening security and preparing to erase threatened facilities. Crusher's sudden physical decline is identified as Cauda. He secretly accepts Doc's irreversible genetic treatment despite the risk of disgrace and exile. Further raids seize a cartel vault and identify the trafficking director as a former regional military colonel, suggesting a disciplined organization rather than unrelated gangs. During an assault on another staging facility, a surface-to-orbit cannon cripples the Phoenix and strands the crew. Omega Force destroys the cannon, breaches the site, and finds that most captives have already been moved. Lucky releases the surviving juveniles, while Cage destroys an incoming cruiser with an improvised missile launch. The crew sanitizes and conceals the Phoenix for later salvage, but the fate of the larger shipment remains unknown.

A rescued juvenile named Andal hides with Omega Force rather than remain with local authorities. Her account reveals a systematic trafficking process involving false registration, medical scans, sorting, and repeated transfers. It also confirms that the regional trafficking organization reports through Cridal. Omega Force takes her off-world and shifts its focus from disrupting individual cartels to identifying the sponsor and purpose behind the abductions. Imperial Intelligence then determines that the Cridal chief of staff is directing the operation without Crisstof Dalton's knowledge and recognizes the regional director as a disavowed former operative. Jason provides evidence that Imperial citizens are among the victims and receives limited intelligence in return. He also learns the truth about Crusher's treatment: Doc has reversed his decline, but the work exposes a concealed system behind the Galvator warrior caste. Jason orders the research destroyed because discovery could endanger both men. With the Phoenix recovered, Omega Force plans a covert assault on the Gates. Abia joins the mission, and the team smuggles the SX-5 into the station under corporate cover.

Cage alters station identity controls while Jason and Crusher move explosives into the Gates. The discovery of twenty to thirty thousand captives forces them to abandon their planned demolition target. A Cridal assassination team attacks Cage, leaving him near death. Lucky gets him stabilized and accepts transfer to a better medical facility, even though the rescuers demand an unspecified future obligation. Jason changes the mission from killing the trafficking director to capturing him for information. He and Crusher enter the cartel sector as security closes in, while Lucky's medical hosts identify him as Combat Unit 777, the same individual once known as Seven. The director tries to escape with a subordinate who instead traps him and reveals himself as Bill Ackerman, an undercover Naval Intelligence Service agent. Ackerman explains that Cridal links many trafficking rings but is not the ultimate organizer. Jason, Crusher, and Ackerman capture the director and flee in an improvised lifeboat as an Esquarian force moves against the Gates. Lucky and Cage depart aboard a private frigate controlled by their unknown hosts, and Lucky warns Jason not to attempt a rescue.

Jason's group escapes with the captured trafficking director and Ackerman's intelligence. A pursuing Cridal special-operations shuttle is disabled and marked for recovery as evidence. Jason delivers the prisoner and Ackerman to Marcus Webb, then obtains a possible lead on Lucky and Cage from the broker who had dealt with Lucky. Webb transfers the prisoner to Esquarian intelligence, where he is designated P9971. Evidence from the recovered shuttle indicates that its team was sent to remove signs of Cridal involvement, while the ultimate trafficking organizer and purpose remain unidentified. The Phoenix is still dismantled for a major rebuild on Satora, so Twingo stays behind and the restored Archive assists with new engineering. Andal remains safely with Abia and has become close to Shira. Jason departs in the SX-5 with Combat Unit 701 to pursue Lucky and Cage, who are alive aboard the outbound frigate but bound to their captors by the price of Cage's treatment. Crisstof Dalton learns that a network within her government ran the operation without her approval and orders an investigation. The responsible official is missing. Carolyn Whitney resumes surveillance of Dalton and prepares to fulfill her longstanding contract to kill her.
